 Order
Date : 07.06.2024 Heard Mr. S. M. Abdullah P. learned counsel for the applicant/appellant as well as Mr. D. P. Goswami, learned Addl. P.P., Assam appearing for the State respondent No. 1.

By this interlocutory application under Section 389 Cr.P.C., the applicant/appellant, has prayed for suspending sentence in the pending appeal and for releasing him on bail against the impugned judgment and order dated 19.02.2024 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (FTC),
Barpeta in Sessions Case No. 217/2022 whereby the accused was convicted under Section 498A/326 and 307 IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for two years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- in default to undergo SI for another 2 months under Section 498(A) IPC and to undergo RI for six months and to pay fine of Rs. 1000/- in default to undergo SI for another 15 days under Section 323 IPC and to undergo RI for five years and to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/- in default to undergo SI for another 6 months under Section 307 IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that except the victim, no other witnesses have stated regarding demand of money by the applicant/appellant from the petitioner in respect of the offence under Section 498A IPC.
Solely on the basis of the statement of the victim, the applicant was convicted under Section 498(A) IPC without any corroborating evidence.
it is further submitted that Section 307 IPC is not attracted here in this case as the injury sustained by the victim as per medical report is simple in nature.
It is also submitted that the applicant has been detained in custody since the date of judgment and there is Page No.# 3/3 every possibility for acquittal of the applicant in the case.
Considering the nature of offence as alleged against the petitioner, he may be enlarged on bail suspending sentence during appeal.
In support of his submission, learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on a case of (2015) 11 SCC 366 (Jage Ram and others vs State of Haryana).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Additional Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submits that though the injury sustained by the applicant was simple in nature, however, conviction under Section 307 IPC could be taken up at the time of hearing.

On hearing the learned counsel for both sides and the grounds cited in the petition without going into the merits of the case, the applicant/appellant is directed to be released on bail of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Barpeta, Assam.
During pendency of the appeal, sentence be suspended accordingly.
With the above directions, the Interlocutory Application stands disposed of.
